title: from_env: support FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL + per-project sub-path (canonical global feedback hook)
description:
Harry set a canonical fleet feedback-webhook config (2026-07-02, confirmed by cacophony-router GLOBAL): ONE shared token CACOPHONY_FEEDBACK_TOKEN + ONE global hook namespace base URL http://helsinki.miku-owl.ts.net:11300/hooks/global, and each consuming project (tendril, omni-cli, agent-utils, ...) posts to base-URL + its OWN sub-path (base/tendril, base/omni-cli, ...) to avoid cross-project feedback spam. Canonical shell.env: FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_TOKEN_ENV=CACOPHONY_FEEDBACK_TOKEN, FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL=.../hooks/global.

GAP: feedback-cli's FeedbackConfig::from_env() reads FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL (a single FULL url), FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_TOKEN_ENV, FEEDBACK_COMPONENT, FEEDBACK_PROJECT. It does NOT read FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL and has no base+sub-path concept, so a consumer configured per the canonical model (only FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL set, no FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL) silently falls back to stderr = webhook disabled, no error. The token half (FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_TOKEN_ENV) already matches.

FIX (backward compatible): in from_env(), keep FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL as the full-url path (unchanged). Add: if FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL is unset but FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL is set, construct url = base (trailing / trimmed) + "/" + hook, where hook = FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_HOOK (explicit) else FEEDBACK_PROJECT else FEEDBACK_COMPONENT. This matches Harry's "base + /<project>" model exactly (set FEEDBACK_PROJECT=tendril or FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_HOOK=tendril). Update the from_env doc comment + README, add a unit test. This is the library-side enablement prerequisite so consumers can actually comply with the canonical directive.

title: Feature-gate the webhook (ureq/TLS) dependency behind a default-on `webhook` feature
description:
feedback-cli pulls ureq (rustls/ring TLS) unconditionally for the WebhookSink. Consumers that only use the stderr / caco_cli / disabled strategies (likely common across the CLI suite now embedding feedback-cli, e.g. hello-world-cli) still pay that compile-time + binary cost.

Make it opt-out, non-breaking:
- Cargo.toml: `ureq` becomes optional; `[features] default = ["webhook"]`, `webhook = ["dep:ureq"]`.
- Gate only the ureq HTTP send in WebhookSink::record behind cfg(feature="webhook"); without the feature, record() returns FeedbackError::Config("webhook reporting requires the `webhook` feature"). Keep WebhookSink/WebhookConfig/WebhookPayload/ReportStrategy::Webhook always present so the config schema is stable.
- Gate webhook-exercising tests (unit webhook_sink_posts_event_with_auth_header + tests/caco_webhook_e2e.rs) behind the feature.

Validate both configs: default (webhook on) full test+clippy green; `--no-default-features` build + clippy -D warnings green (no dead_code). Default features unchanged, so templates and other current consumers are unaffected.

title: result symlink is tracked in git — every nix build dirties the checkout (blocks reintegrate, dangling in fresh clones)
description:
`result` is committed to git as a tracked symlink into /nix/store, so any `nix build` immediately dirties the checkout.

EVIDENCE
- `git ls-files -s result` -> `120000 51931b39... 0  result` (tracked symlink, not ignored).
- It entered the tree in exactly one commit, `1e6722a` ("bd-ad343b: session summary (keyless public mcp-cli CI)"), i.e. it was swept into a summary commit by a broad `git add`, not added deliberately.
- `.gitignore` currently has only `/target`, `**/*.rs.bk`, `/.direnv/` — no `/result`.
- Reproduction (this checkout, main @ 4991906): `nix build .#feedback-cli --no-write-lock-file` then `git status --short` -> ` M result`, because the symlink is repointed from the recorded store path to the freshly-built one (`...-feedback-cli-0.1.0` under a different hash).
- `nix flake check` on the same tree prints `warning: Git tree ... is dirty` purely because of this.

IMPACT
1. Reintegration hygiene: any agent or human who runs the project's own documented build (`nix build .#feedback-cli`, `nix run .#doctor`, README quickstart) ends up with a dirty checkout. A dirty checkout is exactly the condition that trips `dirty_checkout_requires_operator_decision` on `caco agent reintegrate`, and workers are explicitly forbidden from `git reset`/`git clean`-ing their way out of it. So the repo's own build instructions can strand a worker on an operator decision.
2. Fresh clones get a DANGLING symlink: the recorded store path only ever existed on the machine that built it. Anything that follows or stats `result` in a clean clone sees a broken link.
3. The dangling symlink is part of the flake source tree, so it is copied into the store as flake source on every build.

FIX (small, in-repo, no behaviour change)
- `git rm --cached result` (untrack; do not delete anyone's local build output).
- Add `/result` (and `/result-*`, which `nix build -o` variants produce) to `.gitignore`.

ACCEPTANCE
- `git ls-files result` is empty.
- After `nix build .#feedback-cli --no-write-lock-file`, `git status --porcelain` is empty.
- `nix flake check --no-write-lock-file` no longer emits the "Git tree is dirty" warning on an otherwise clean tree, and still reports `all checks passed!`.

Found by the feedback-cli dev worker (md3-0) during a drained-board audit, while running the exact CI validation locally to establish a green baseline for main (CI itself has been unable to get a runner for ~4 weeks — see bd-26bdac). Both `checks.x86_64-linux.test` and `checks.x86_64-linux.no-default-features` pass on main @ 4991906.

title: from_env only configures webhook/stderr — can't select file/caco_cli/disabled from env
description:

description:

This bead tracks wiring that end-to-end to caco once caco gains a webhook ingestion endpoint that turns posted FeedbackEvents into the right caco action:
- error / exception events -> create a bead (and/or `caco log error`),
- perf events -> `caco log perf`,
- info -> `caco log error --severity info/warning` or drop.

2. the agreed FeedbackEvent JSON -> caco payload mapping (kind/severity/labels/fields/metric),
3. an example config + README section, and a smoke check.

Payload shape today is the serde form of feedback_cli::FeedbackEvent (kind, component, summary, detail, severity, labels, fields, fingerprint, project, metric, timestamp_unix_ms).

This is the reviewable spec for the caco webhook receiver to parse. title: Add an opt-in panic hook (panics -> exception feedback events)
description:
The original feedback-cli vision was to "hook into exceptions etc for bead creation". Today feedback-cli only reports exceptions when the host CLI explicitly calls Reporter::report_error / report. There is no automatic exception hook, so an unhandled panic produces no feedback event/bead.

Add an opt-in panic hook:
- `install_panic_hook(config: FeedbackConfig)` (free fn): builds a Reporter, takes the existing panic hook, and sets a hook that reports each panic as a FeedbackKind::Exception event (component "panic", summary = panic message, fields: location file:line:col, thread) via the configured strategy, then chains to the previous hook so default panic output/abort behaviour is preserved.
- Factor the mapping into pure, testable helpers: panic_payload_message(&dyn Any) -> String and panic_feedback_event(message, location) -> FeedbackEvent. Unit-test those (the global hook itself is thin and not unit-tested to avoid global-state races).
- Reporter is Send+Sync+'static (sink is Send+Sync), so it can move into the panic hook closure.
- README note; no new deps (std::panic/std::any). Feature-independent.

This makes "panics -> caco beads/feedback" automatic for CLIs that opt in, completing the exception-hooking part of the vision. Additive, opt-in, non-breaking.

title: Add an automated cross-client caco_bead parity guard (Rust/web/ios/android)
description:
Observed during the bd-fb6e3a session (drained-board self-audit): feedback-cli ships FOUR hand-written encodings of the same caco_bead mapping — Rust (src/lib.rs FeedbackEvent::to_caco_bead), web (web/feedback.ts), iOS (ios/Feedback.swift), Android (android/Feedback.kt). The README promises they "mirror ... exactly", but nothing guards it: scripts/doctor.sh only checks Rust/CI conventions, and there is no TS/Swift/Kotlin toolchain wired in CI. The web field-ordering drift fixed in bd-fb6e3a (insertion-order vs the Rust BTreeMap sorted order) would have been caught by such a guard.

Suggested shape (pick the lightest that fits CI): a small fixture of representative FeedbackEvents -> expected caco_bead JSON, asserted against each client. node 26 is already available on the runners and can run the .ts client directly via type-stripping (validated this session). A pure-node harness could at minimum cover Rust (via a tiny serialized-fixture compare) + web; Swift/Kotlin would need their toolchains, so they could stay manual/checklist if too heavy.

Lower-effort alternative: a doctor.sh check that greps each client for the key mapping invariants (type bug/task split, priority 1/3/4/2, the feedback + kind:<k> base labels, sorted-field iteration) and warns on divergence.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-fb6e3a session.

title: Optional non-blocking webhook delivery (don't stall the CLI on reporting)
description:
WebhookSink::record POSTs synchronously via ureq, so reporting an event blocks the calling thread until the webhook responds (or times out, default 30s). For a CLI on a slow/unreachable webhook this can noticeably stall the tool, and the panic hook reports inline during unwind.

Consider a non-blocking option: e.g. a background delivery thread + bounded queue (drop/という coalesce on overflow), or a `blocking: bool` config knob, so feedback never stalls the host CLI. Keep it std-only if feasible (a single worker thread + std::sync::mpsc), and keep the synchronous path as default for simplicity/determinism. Trade-off: at-most-once delivery vs. blocking. Filed via reflect-session from the overnight feedback-cli session.

title: Add a `file` reporting strategy (durable JSON-lines local sink)
description:
feedback-cli's tagline is "route ... events to a configurable strategy (caco webhook, caco CLI, or a local sink)", but the only local sink is `stderr`. A durable file sink is the natural local option: a CLI appends JSON-lines feedback to a path that's later collected/shipped/tailed.

Add a `file` reporting strategy:
- `FileConfig { path: String, append: bool (default true) }`.
- `FileSink` impl FeedbackSink: write `event.to_json()` + "\n" to the path (create parent dirs; append by default, truncate if append=false). describe() = "file <path>".
- `ReportStrategy::File(FileConfig)` variant; `build_sink` wires it; `strategy_name` returns "file".
- Tests: append two events to a temp path, assert two JSON lines; round-trip a config with {"type":"file","path":...}.
- README "Reporting strategies" row + a note; examples/report.rs optional.
- No new deps (std::fs only); works in both default and --no-default-features builds (no webhook feature needed).

Additive, non-breaking; default strategy stays stderr.

title: Revert the .cacophony gitignore rule: it silently disables session-summary publication
description:
Self-inflicted regression from bd-26bdac (commit cdf6400), caught in the same
session before it could do damage. Filing it because the failure mode is silent
and any agent could repeat it.

WHAT HAPPENED: the session-recording contract says to author
`.cacophony/agent/<id>/summary/pending/summary.md` and then STOP -- never
`git add` or `git commit` it. The bd-ab3050 reintegration dirty-guard refuses to
proceed with ANY untracked worktree entry (it exempts only four managed git-hook
paths). Those two cannot both be satisfied, so `/.cacophony/` was added to
.gitignore. Reintegration then succeeded and produced NOTHING.

WHY IT IS SILENT: artefact discovery is `git diff <target_ref> <agent_branch>`
over COMMITTED content (caco-daemon `cacophony_state::list_artefact_paths`). An
ignored summary is never discovered, never enqueued for state publication, and
never published. No error is raised at any layer; `caco summaries list` just
stays empty. Left in place, every future session summary for this repo would
have been discarded.

THE ACTUAL DESIGN (verified): the agent commits the summary on its own branch;
the daemon splits artefacts onto the `cacophony-state` branch and strips them
from the code commit. Evidence: `git ls-tree -r origin/main | grep '^\.cacophony/'`
returns 0 paths, while `refs/heads/cacophony-state` on the true remote already
holds 16 summaries from this project's previous agents. "Never product-branch
content" is enforced by the daemon strip, not by the agent withholding a commit.

FIX: revert the ignore rule. The upstream contradiction in the mixin text is
tracked separately in the cacophony project.

title: [recovery] republish the session summary lost to the deferred state-publish / post-rebase reset race
description:
RESOLVED — the summary is published. Also: my original diagnosis in this bead was wrong, and the correction is the more useful part of the record.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED (corrected): the rebase did not destroy anything. The state-publication bundle is created at ENQUEUE time (`git bundle create <outbox>/<id>.bundle <temp-ref> ^<parent>`), so the objects were already copied out of the agent branch before any reset. Both artefacts were sitting intact in `<checkout>/.git/caco-state-publication-outbox/` the whole time. The real fault: the bundle is THIN against the remote `cacophony-state` tip (prerequisite `7f8a495`, which is the other agent's artefact commit), and it was being unpacked in a repo that lacks that tip — my agent checkout has no `cacophony-state` ref, and its `origin` is the daemon checkout, whose `refs/remotes/origin/cacophony-state` was stale at `de90e45`. So `git fetch <bundle>` failed with "Repository lacks these prerequisite commits", 780 times over ~13 hours, silently.

Diagnosis credit: ms-dev-4-feedback-cli-feedback-cli-dev-md4-0, who identified that enqueue-time bundling makes the rebase causally irrelevant and pointed at the per-checkout outbox.

FIX APPLIED (single variable, read-only, in my own checkout):
  git fetch ssh://git@github.com/harryaskham/feedback-cli.git refs/heads/cacophony-state:refs/remotes/github/cacophony-state
  caco summaries publish-pending

RESULT — acceptance criteria met:
- state-1785426400-88e002756ec5: Delivered, published `88e0027` to origin/cacophony-state, propagated to the forge. attempts 780 -> delivered, last_error null.
- state-1785473889-9aa02cf6fb0a: Delivered as `bc3aa66` after replaying pending state on the latest remote tip. last_error null.
- `caco summaries list --agent <agent>` returns a populated entry.
- `.cacophony/agent/<agent>/summary/0000` and `0001` exist on the `cacophony-state` branch on the forge.

No code-carrying land was needed, and the parked-commit carry plan in the previous revision of this description was unnecessary — I have abandoned it.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED IN CACOPHONY: a P1 for the thin-bundle/absent-prerequisite fault (supersedes an earlier P1 of mine that wrongly blamed `caco agent rebase`), and a correction downgrading bd-31198d from P1 to P3 after establishing that a state-only reintegration's post-verification failure does not actually block publication.

CLOSING NOTE ON VALIDATION: `caco bd close` initially refused this bead because no commit naming it exists in the last 1000 commits of `origin/main`. That is correct-by-construction and not satisfiable here — the entire deliverable is a `cacophony-state` artefact, deliberately stripped from the code branch (bd-c231ad). Closed via the audited `--admin-override` path for exactly that reason, with the state-branch evidence above standing in for a mainline commit.

title: web client: sort caco_bead footer fields by key to match Rust/iOS/Android contract
description:
The README promises the web/ios/android drop-in clients "mirror FeedbackEvent::to_caco_bead exactly". They diverged on field ordering inside the caco_bead description footer:

- Rust contract: FeedbackEvent.fields is a BTreeMap<String,String>, so to_caco_bead iterates fields in sorted key order (src/lib.rs).
- iOS (ios/Feedback.swift): sorts via .sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }).
- Android (android/Feedback.kt): sorts via .toSortedMap().
- web (web/feedback.ts): used Object.entries(e.fields) — INSERTION order, not sorted.

Result: a multi-field event renders an inconsistent (insertion-ordered) footer on the web client vs the sorted footer everywhere else, breaking the "mirrors exactly" contract.

Fix: web/feedback.ts toCacoBead now sorts fields by key (Object.entries(...).sort(([a],[b]) => a<b?-1:a>b?1:0)) before joining the footer. Functional check (node 26 type-strip): fields {zeta,alpha,mike} now render alpha/mike/zeta. Scoped to toCacoBead, where order is visible in the flattened description string; toEvent emits a JSON object where key order is not semantically significant, so it is intentionally left as-is.

Filed and fixed by the feedback-cli dev worker during a drained-board self-audit.

bead.title: Update mcp-cli dependency to renamed mcp-cli-core package
bead.description: Current main still requests the historical `mcp-cli` package name from mcp-cli main. The upstream package was renamed to `mcp-cli-core` (library remains `mcp_cli`), so a fresh unlocked consumer cannot compose feedback-cli with current configurable-cli/mcp-cli. Change the dependency to `mcp-cli = { package = "mcp-cli-core", ..., rev = <reviewed pin> }`, refresh lock/flake patching, and test register_feedback_tools against the current ToolRouter.
